content.text: {"persuasion":"PERSUADED","support_scope":"FULL","rationale":"The book's core claim — that 'works' names deeds as such, a neutral term distinct from obedience, with obedience/disobedience being the deed's relation to a legitimate or rival command, and with Paul's excluded 'work' in Romans 4 being labor presented for wages rather than obedience per se — is carried directly by its cited texts. Romans 4:4 supplies the economic frame explicitly ('the reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt'); Luke 17:7-10 supplies the decisive complement, that even complete commanded obedience yields no wage claim ('we are unprofitable servants: we have done that which was our duty to do'); Exodus 18:20 shows 'the work that they must do' taught alongside ordinances, laws, and the way to walk — a deed-word coordinated with command-words rather than identical to them; Micah 6:16 shows 'evil works' as the kept statutes of Omri and Ahab, i.e., deeds classified as evil by the rival command they execute, exactly the book's mechanism; James 2:21-22 shows the same deed-word functioning as faith made visible. The strongest specific counter — the mainstream evidential reading in which works are the outward fruit disclosing the inner state, and 'not of works' excludes human deeds generally as a saving instrument — agrees that works are deeds and so does not contradict the book's core referent; it disputes only precision and mechanism. Moreover the book's account explains details the fruit-framing leaves loose: why Luke 17:10 denies wage after complete obedience (a fact awkward if 'works' simply means obedience offered for salvation), why Micah's evil works are 'kept' like statutes, why works can be 'kept' at all (Rev 2:26), and why Paul can exclude works in Ephesians 2:9 and command them in 2:10 without contradiction. No supplied text is better explained by the counter, so the book's identification stands as the best-supported explanation.","book_core_identification":"'Works' means deeds — a neutral term for human actions — and is not a synonym for obedience: a work becomes obedience when it executes a legitimate command and disobedience when the deed or its commanding authority conflicts with God's command; the 'work' Paul excludes in Romans 4 is defined by its economic claim (labor presented for wages, making God a debtor), not deeds or obedience as such, since even complete obedience earns no wage (Luke 17:10), while James 2 uses the same deed-word for faith made visible.","book_secondary_elaborations":["The occurrence-by-occurrence classification of Paul's erga nomou ('works of the law') in The End of the Law — some occurrences God's law explicitly, some the circumcision-party's application, some ambiguous","The claim that works are 'commandment-shaped' and therefore can be 'kept' (Rev 2:26; Ps 111:7 pairing God's works with His commandments)","The larger telos-of-the-law argument: Christ as the law's purpose rather than its termination, the named-laws table, and the readings of Colossians 2, Ephesians 2:15, Hebrews 7-9, Romans 14, Acts 15","The textual note on Romans 9:32 (TR 'works of the law' vs. critical text 'as if by works')","The chapter-6 framework distinguishing love, knowing, faith, belief, and faithfulness as offices of one covenant response"],"strongest_counter_interpretation":"The mainstream evidential/fruit reading (Responses A-C primary meaning): 'works' are the outward deeds that express and evidence the inner spiritual condition — good works the necessary fruit of grace and living faith, evil works the fruit of the flesh or darkness — and in Paul's polemic 'works' stands for human doing (including obedience) insofar as it is offered as the ground or instrument of justification, which is excluded in favor of faith alone; works then function evidentially at judgment because they manifest the heart.","counter_core_identification":"'Works' are a person's deeds understood essentially as fruit and evidence of the inner state (faith/grace vs. flesh/unbelief), with Paul's 'not of works' excluding human deeds generally — obedience included — as any instrument of justification.","counter_relation_to_book_core":"SAME_CORE_BROADER","material_core_denial":"To materially deny the book's core, the counter would have to hold that 'works' intrinsically means obedience or moral performance — that the word itself carries the evaluative and soteriological freight — so that Romans 4 sets faith against obedience as such, making obedience itself the wage-claiming rival of grace. Both identifications cannot be true of the same referent: either 'work' is a neutral deed-word whose master, command-relation, and wage-claim are supplied by context, or 'work' is by definition obedience/self-effort excluded from salvation.","counter_case":["Ephesians 2:8-10 and Titus 3:5 exclude works from salvation in general terms, which the counter reads as excluding all human doing, obedience included, as the instrument of justification","Matthew 7:16-20 and Galatians 5:19-23 present deeds as fruit revealing the tree, supporting the evidential framing as the word's primary force","Romans 4:4-5, on the counter's reading, sets 'him that worketh' against 'him that believeth' as a direct faith-versus-doing antithesis, not merely a wage-claim antithesis","Revelation 20:12-13 and Romans 2:6 make works the basis of judgment because they manifest the heart, which the evidential reading explains naturally","Isaiah 64:6, Romans 9:32, and Philippians 3:9 support the polemical extension in which 'works' stands for self-righteous human effort as a category"],"book_explanatory_advantages":["Romans 4:4's own vocabulary is economic — 'reward... reckoned... of debt' — the text defines the excluded work by its wage claim, exactly as the book says, rather than by its being obedience","Luke 17:7-10 is fully explained: complete performance of everything commanded still earns no wage, showing obedience per se is not what Paul's wage-frame excludes; the counter must treat this text as tangential","Micah 6:16's 'works of the house of Ahab' kept as statutes is precisely a deed classified evil by the rival command it executes — the book's mechanism stated in the text itself","Exodus 18:20 coordinates 'the work that they must do' with ordinances, laws, and the way to walk, showing 'work' as the deed-word alongside command-words at the law's first teaching","The book explains why works can be 'kept' with the commandment-keeping verb (Rev 2:26) and why Psalm 111:7 pairs God's works with His commandments","It reconciles Ephesians 2:9 with 2:10 and Titus 3:5 with 3:8 without tension: works excluded as purchase price, restored as the created life — the exclusion targets the claim, not the deed","It resolves Romans 4 against James 2 cleanly: the same deed-word appears in a wage-frame in one and a faith-enactment frame in the other, so no contradiction between 'not of works' and 'justified by works' arises"],"counter_explanatory_advantages":["The fruit/evidence framing directly explains judgment-by-works texts (Rev 20:12-13; Rom 2:6) and tree/fruit texts (Matt 7:16-20) as deeds manifesting the heart","It matches the broad polemical usage in Romans 9:32 and Philippians 3:9 where 'works' shorthand for self-righteous striving reads naturally","It is the settled cross-tradition reading and requires no fine-grained lexical distinction between work and obedience"],"evidence_book_core_cannot_explain":[],"comparative_winner":"BOOK","decisive_sources":["Romans 4:4-5 (the excluded work is defined by wages and debt, in the text's own words)","Luke 17:7-10 (complete obedience to all that was commanded still creates no wage claim — duty, not payment)","Exodus 18:20 (the work to be done taught alongside ordinances, laws, and the way to walk, at the law's first teaching)","Micah 6:16 (evil works as the kept statutes of Omri and works of the house of Ahab — deeds made evil by the rival command executed)","James 2:21-22 (Abraham's work as faith wrought with works and made perfect by them)","Psalm 111:7 with Revelation 2:26 (works paired with commandments; works 'kept' with the commandment-keeping verb)","Ephesians 2:8-10 (works excluded as source, immediately restored as the created life)"],"unresolved_objections":["The evidential/fruit framing of the common interpretation is not refuted by the book and remains true alongside it; the book's entry does not deny that deeds evidence the inner state, so the two framings coexist rather than one eliminating the other","Whether the sharp 'not a synonym for obedience' distinction holds uniformly across every Pauline occurrence (e.g., Galatians 3:10, where the issue is doing 'all things written in the book of the law') is argued in The End of the Law but depends on occurrence-by-occurrence classification a skeptic could contest","The polemical Protestant usage in which 'works' stands for self-righteous effort as a category (Rom 9:32; Phil 3:9; Isa 64:6) captures real texts; the book subsumes these under the wage-claim analysis, which is plausible but not the only possible reading of Romans 9:32 given its textual variant","The book's downstream conclusions about the continuing force of the law (Colossians 2, sabbath, appointed times) go well beyond the works entry itself and are not established merely by the entry's core being correct"],"confidence":"medium"}
